title: Reliance Foundation to Build Lifelong Home for 5,000 in Karjat
excerpt: Nita Ambani laid the foundation stone on November 1 for Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, a roughly 100-acre, not-for-profit township for orphaned children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
body:
• Reliance Foundation announced Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray on November 1, 2026, a lifelong, not-for-profit home in Karjat, near Mumbai, for orphaned children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
  • The roughly 100-acre township is planned for more than 5,000 residents, and about 15,000 people in total including caregivers, medical professionals, support staff and their families.
  • It will be built in multiple phases, subject to approvals, as eight residential villages with family-style homes, a hospital, a temple, schools, rehabilitation centres and workshops.
  • For diaspora families weighing long-term care for ageing parents or a disabled family member in India, this is an announcement to watch — no admission process, timeline or fee details have been published yet.

Reliance Foundation will establish Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, a lifelong home for orphaned children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, at Karjat near Mumbai. Founder and Chairperson Nita Ambani performed the Bhumi Pujan and laid the foundation stone for the project on Sunday, November 1, according to the Foundation's announcement carried by ANI.

The institution is envisioned as permanent and not-for-profit. It will span approximately 100 acres and take shape in multiple phases, subject to the requisite approvals, the announcement said. No completion date was given.

"For me and my family, Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray is a beginning very close to our hearts. It is a step towards building a loving home for people with disabilities, children who need a home and seniors who seek care and comfort."

— Nita Ambani, Founder and Chairperson, Reliance Foundation

Who It Is For, and How It Will Be Organised

The township is designed to provide a lifelong home to more than 5,000 residents, including people with developmental disabilities, orphaned children and senior citizens. Together with caregivers, medical professionals, support staff and their families, it is expected to support a community of approximately 15,000 people, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

Residents will live in small, family-style homes supported by dedicated house parents and caregivers, according to the announcement. The township will comprise eight residential villages, each named after a sacred river of India, each with its own colour, symbol and sensory garden intended to help residents navigate their surroundings.

Every resident will have an individualised care and development plan, prepared in consultation with them and their families and reviewed at least every six months, the Foundation said. The plans are to cover healthcare, education, skills, employment, friendships and personal well-being, coordinated by a dedicated key worker.

Facilities Named in the Announcement

The announcement lists a specialised hospital, rehabilitation centres, inclusive schools, sports facilities, a temple, playgrounds, gardens, farms and workshops. It also names an animal companionship farm, vocational spaces including a bakery, café and craft studios, family respite homes, mobile medical clinics, a national training academy for disability-care professionals, and a hospice wing with a garden of remembrance.

Those facilities are part of the plan as announced; the Foundation has not published a phase-by-phase construction schedule. The temple, hospital, sports facilities and cafés are also envisioned to serve neighbouring villages. Approximately 1,000 people from the surrounding region are expected to access therapy, education and employment opportunities, with others reached through respite care, outreach programmes and community healthcare.

"As a mother, my deepest hope is that parents who have spent a lifetime worrying about who will care for their children when they are no longer there can find peace in knowing that their child will always have a home and a family of their own."

— Nita Ambani, Founder and Chairperson, Reliance Foundation

Why This Matters Beyond Mumbai

The announcement speaks directly to a question many families — including NRI families — struggle to answer: who provides lifelong, specialist care for a disabled relative when parents age or die, or for a senior who needs continuous support? The Foundation framed Anant Ashray as an answer for people with developmental disabilities, cerebral palsy, autism, epilepsy and complex medical conditions, particularly those requiring continuous specialist care that can be difficult to access outside major cities.

The initiative is presented as an extension of Reliance Foundation's 'We Care' philosophy, under the line "A Home for Every Life."

What Is Not Yet Known

The announcement does not state when the first residents will move in, how admissions will work, what it will cost residents or families, or how places will be allocated. Those details will matter for any family considering it. Readers should watch for further announcements from Reliance Foundation rather than rely on summaries — and treat any admission or fee claim that does not come from the Foundation itself with caution.
nri_angle: A lifelong-care institution in India relevant to NRI families planning long-term care for ageing parents or disabled relatives back home; admission and fee details are not yet published.
